status_legend.VERIFIED_PRIMARY: Read from the primary or official text itself (NCC page, council DCP text in the JCE library)
status_legend.VERIFIED_SECONDARY: Read from a council guideline, government agency page or other document that quotes a standard; the owner must check against the standard
status_legend.UNVERIFIED: Could not be confirmed from an accessible primary or official source; do not rely on the value

_meta.topic: Accessible parking, NCC 2022 Volume One D4D6 and AS/NZS 2890.6

ncc_edition.value: NCC 2022 (Volume One, Amendment 1 consolidated, 1 May 2023 and later amendments)
ncc_edition.note: Trade press (article dated 25/03/2026) states NSW defers adoption of NCC 2025 to 1 May 2027, so NCC 2022 remains the edition in force in NSW at 13/11/2026. Owner should confirm against the NSW Planning Portal / ABCB state adoption table.

spaces_required.clause: NCC 2022 Volume One D4D6(2); formerly Table D3.5 in NCC 2016/2019
spaces_required.rule_text: Number of accessible spaces is by building class and total carparking spaces provided, calculated separately for each classification in a multi-classified building (D4D6 commentary).

value.ratio: 1 accessible space for every 100 carparking spaces or part thereof
1 accessible space for every 50 carparking spaces or part thereof up to 1000 spaces, then 1 additional space for each further 100 spaces or part thereof
1 accessible space for every 100 carparking spaces or part thereof

class_7b_warehouse_storage.clause: D4D6(2) Class 5, 7, 8 or 9c (D4D6 names Class 7 without a 7a or 7b split)
class_7b_warehouse_storage.note: Class 7 as a whole is listed; the page text does not separate 7a and 7b.

value.ratio: 1 accessible space for every 100 carparking spaces or part thereof

worked_examples_for_tool.note: Derived from the ratios above, not quoted from the NCC. Class 5/7/8: ceil(n/100). Class 6: ceil(n/50) for n up to 1000.

mixed_class_rule.value: Count accessible spaces separately for the spaces serving each classification of a multi-classified building

where_required.value: D4D6(1)(a): in a Class 7a building required to be accessible, and in a carparking area on the same allotment as a building required to be accessible. Class 5, 6, 7b, 8 and 9a buildings must be accessible to and within all areas normally used by occupants (D4D2(6)).
where_required.note: Paraphrased. Applies to carparking on the allotment of an accessible Class 7b or 8 unit as well.

parking_service_exemption.value: No accessible spaces needed where a parking service is used and the public has no direct access to the spaces

value.text: Accessible spaces need not be identified with signage where there are not more than 5 carparking spaces in total

sign_exemption_small_car_park.note: Only the signage requirement is relaxed per the page text read; whether a space must still be provided at 5 or fewer spaces follows the D4D6(2) ratios (1 space for 1 to 100 spaces).

ncc_edition_of_2890_6_called_up.value: AS/NZS 2890.6:2009 (per two NSW accessibility reports and Griffith DCP written against NCC 2022)
ncc_edition_of_2890_6_called_up.note: Schedule 4 was not retrievable. AS 2890.6:2022 was published 11/11/2022 and supersedes the 2009 edition (https://www.intertekinform.com/en-au/standards/as-2890-6-2022-129723_saig_as_as_3198172/). The owner must confirm which edition the NCC Schedule of Referenced Documents calls up.

deferral.value: The NCC Volume One Part D4 DTS provisions are written to meet the Disability (Access to Premises - Buildings) Standards 2010 (Cth). A building solution must also satisfy the Premises Standards, including their exemptions and concessions. Where the NCC and the Standards differ, the Standards prevail as Commonwealth legislation.
deferral.clause: NCC 2022 Vol One D4 introduction and "NCC Blurbs" text (Tasmanian variation wording read)
deferral.note: The wording read came from a page section noted as relating to the Tasmanian variation; the national position was not isolated. The statement that the Standards prevail is general legal position and is UNVERIFIED here. Check the Standards at legislation.gov.au (Schedule 1 Access Code, D3.5).

premises_standards.standards_url: https://www.legislation.gov.au/ (Disability (Access to Premises - Buildings) Standards 2010, Access Code Part D3, clause D3.5) NOT RETRIEVED

as_nzs_2890_6_dimensions_2009_edition._note: 2009 edition values quoted by a draft of the standard (APH exhibit), a NSW council access report and the Griffith DCP. Australian-only values apply (the standard has separate New Zealand values).

dedicated_bay.clause: AS/NZS 2890.6:2009 cl 2.2.1 ("In Australia, 2400 mm wide by 5400 mm long")
dedicated_bay.note: The APH document is a DRAFT; owner must verify against the published standard.

shared_area_at_end_of_bay.clause: cl 2.2.1(c) per draft; also Melton Car Parking Guidelines 2015 p21 Figures 20-21

same_level.value: Dedicated and shared areas at the same level

value.position: central in the shared area, shown in Figures 2.2 and 2.3

bollard_in_shared_area.clause: cl 2.2.1(e) "bollards shall be provided in the positions shown in Figures 2.2 and 2.3" (draft); 800 plus or minus 50 mm from a NSW access report summary
bollard_in_shared_area.note: Height is not given consistently: see bollard_height_candidates.

bollard_height_candidates.clause: AS/NZS 2890.6 bollard clause not read directly
bollard_height_candidates.note: Two secondary sources agree on 1300 mm minimum height; the Karratha guideline may be quoting the 2022 edition. Not confirmed from the standard.

headroom.source_url: https://aphref.aph.gov.au/house/committee/laca/disabilitystandards/exhibits/exhibit11.pdf ; Griffith DCP No 20 cl 1.9.6 (2.5 m clear height)
headroom.clause: cl 2.x headroom (draft); user brief of 2.5 m is consistent

value.bituminous_outdoor_note: 1:33 allowed for bituminous seal outdoors per a NSW access report summary

value.symbol: International Symbol of Access, 800 to 1000 mm high on a blue rectangle up to 1200 mm
value.symbol_position: 500 to 600 mm from the entry point of the space
value.shared_area_hatching: strips 150 to 200 mm wide at 45 degrees, spaced 200 to 300 mm apart, in the non-trafficked part of the shared area; not required where a driveway is used as the shared area
value.bay_line_colour_and_hatch_colour: yellow hatching per blog, not confirmed

value.post_sign: International Symbol of Access sign visible from approach, at accessible bay

signage.clause: not read from AS 2890.6 or AS 1742.11
signage.note: Blog only. The only NCC signage text read is the 5-space exemption in D4D6(1)(d).

location.value: Within 50 m of an accessible entrance (Melton guideline); NCC commentary says as close as possible to the main pedestrian entrance
location.note: The 50 m figure is a Victorian council guideline, not NCC.

as_2890_6_2022_edition_candidates._note: Published 11/11/2022 and supersedes AS/NZS 2890.6:2009. The only dimensions found are in a WA council guideline and they differ from 2009. Do not use unless the owner confirms the edition called up by NCC 2022 (or Premises Standards) and checks the dimensions.

angled_space.note: Edition not stated by the council; values differ from the 2400 x 5400 mm in the 2009 edition.

tool_defaults_recommended.note: Defaults follow the user brief and the 2009 edition values; owner to verify (see ncc_edition_of_2890_6_called_up).
